en: Dissolving calamansi juice and sugar in water creates a homogeneous solution known locally as fresh calamansi juice.
Steaming puto batter causes a chemical change that transforms the liquid rice flour mixture into a solid, fluffy cake.
Crushing pork chicharon into smaller pieces is a physical change because the chemical composition of the fried pork remains identical.
Abaca fibers possess exceptional tensile strength and saltwater resistance, making them an ideal natural material for marine ropes in the Philippines.
Halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture because you can easily see and separate its distinct solid ingredients, like sweet beans and ube, from the milk.
Salt farmers in Bolinao use solar evaporation to separate solid salt crystals from liquid seawater trapped in shallow coastal ponds.
Carbon dioxide gas is dissolved under pressure in Philippine soft drinks, escaping as visible bubbles when you open the sealed plastic bottle.
Making ice candy involves a physical change where liquid fruit juice freezes into solid ice inside sealed plastic tubes.
Traditional Filipino cooks use a wooden sandok because wood is a poor thermal conductor that prevents the cook's hands from burning.
The metal body of an old jeepney undergoes a chemical change called oxidation when exposed to rain, forming flaky orange rust.
Extracting virgin coconut oil involves letting a liquid mixture settle so the lighter oil floats on top of the heavier water.
Mother-of-pearl shells from Palawan are polished for jewelry because their hard, solid calcium carbonate structure resists scratching and breaking.
